{"decision":"`import_graph` writes a node whose `node_ref` property names a node that is in neither the document nor the graph, and names it on `ImportReport.dangling_node_refs` (printed by `--import`). It does NOT fail the import. `create_node` is unchanged and still refuses such a write outright.

Recorded as PROPOSED: it was Claude's engineering call, taken to keep this design's own export restorable, and it is Anthony's to settle or overturn.","name":"A restore reports an unresolvable node reference rather than refusing the whole document","rationale":"THE ALTERNATIVE, and why it lost: refuse the import, matching `create_node`. Measured 2026-08-29 — this design's own export carries nine references written before the guard existed (five instances of a `prj:`/`proj:` typo, four capabilities renamed after the fact was written). Under refusal the export could not be restored AT ALL, and the only remedy on offer was hand-editing the export document, which is the one thing this project tells users never to do. Any user upgrading into the guard with a single pre-existing dangling reference would silently acquire an unrestorable backup.

THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES IT: a write ASSERTS something new, and refusing a new record about a node the design does not have is right. An import ASSERTS NOTHING — it reproduces a state that already existed, and the document is the evidence that it did. Refusing there is the tool substituting its judgement for a reality it is being handed.

NOT A NEW POLICY. `ImportReport` had already answered this same question three times — `skipped_edges` (an edge whose endpoint is missing is skipped and named, not fatal), `integrity_note` and `provenance_note`, each documented as "the import still proceeds but never silently". A dangling property reference is the other shape of a missing endpoint, so answering it differently would have one import refusing what its neighbour two lines up reports.

THE COST, stated plainly: import is now a path by which a dangling reference can enter a graph that did not have one — an export/import laundering route the write guard closes. Judged acceptable because it requires a deliberately constructed document, and because the renames that produce most real dangles are unreachable by ANY write-time check and need detection over the graph as it stands. That detection is a separate open piece of work.","status":"proposed"}
